predecessors.name: Austrian Empire
predecessors.text: Carniola, Gorizia and Gradisca, Trieste, Istria, the Croatian lands southwest of the Sava, western Carinthia and East Tyrol: the Austrian cession of the Treaty of Schonbrunn

predecessors.name: Italian Republic (Kingdom of Italy from 1805)
predecessors.text: Dalmatia, Ragusa and Cattaro, passed from the Kingdom of Italy

successors.text: The Illyrian Provinces, 'confirmed' to Austria by the Congress of Vienna (formal annexation 9 June 1815); in 1816 reconstituted as the Kingdom of Illyria without Dalmatia and Croatia but with all…

ledger.x: 14 October 1809: the Illyrian Provinces are created at Schonbrunn.
1810: Dalmatia, Istria and Ragusa pass from the Kingdom of Italy to the Illyrian Provinces.
Autumn 1813: Austria overruns the northern provinces.
6 December 1813: Zara surrenders to Austrian and British forces after a 34-day siege.
3 January 1814: the French garrison at Kotor surrenders.
ledger.cp: British naval forces and Montenegrin insurgents

ledger.x: 27 January 1814: the French garrison at Ragusa surrenders.

January 1814: French rule in Illyria ends; Austria holds the provinces until the Congress of Vienna confirms them ('formal annexation by the Austrian Empire: 9 June 1815'), and the Treaty of Paris (30 May 1814) reduced France to its 1792 borders.

wars.name: Austrian campaign in the Illyrian Provinces
wars.outcome: Austria declared war in August 1813, took Trieste (29 October 1813), Zara (6 December 1813), Kotor (3 January 1814) and Ragusa (27 January 1814), ending French rule; the Congress of Vienna confirmed the provinces to Austria (9 June 1815).

certainty.note: The Schonbrunn cession names provinces and cities, not a surveyed line; the Military Frontier and the Dalmatian hinterland are approximate, and the 1813 reconquest is dated for only four places.
